results.finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::partial/inconsistent fix for value fidelity: only date/timestamp/timestamptz are pinned to raw postgres text, while other pg types that the default parser turns into js objects still flow through and end up json-stringified into sheet cells. the change's own e2e expectations enshrine this: bytea renders as `{"type":"buffer","data":[222,173,190,239]}`, interval as `{"years":1,"months":2,"days":3}`, circle as `{"x":1,"y":2,"radius":3}`. if the intent is "cells show the value the database shows", these are user-visible wrong values left unaddressed; if the intent is only the timezone shift, the accepted json-blob rendering should be a stated decision (in the design doc) rather than an incidental test expectation.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in datasource.service.ts:20-24 that RAW_TEXT_OIDS covers only DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ, and datasourceTypeParser delegates all other OIDs to the default pg parser, so BYTEA/INTERVAL/CIRCLE/JSON/array values still arrive as JS objects. readonly.ts:32-36 (toCell) JSON-stringifies any non-null object and loadQueryResults writes that into the cell, so those types render as JSON blobs rather than the Postgres text representation; the new e2e table in database.e2e-spec.ts encodes exactly those expectations ('{"type":"Buffer",...}', '{"years":1,...}', '{"x":1,"y":2,"radius":3}'), confirming the claim's reading. It is therefore a genuine, if partial, fidelity gap rather than a misreading. I rate it minor because toCell is still an improvement over the previous String(val) ([object Object]) and the affected types are uncommon in typical query results; the "should be documented in the design doc" portion I could not verify.
